title: Migrate Rust num-parser from panic-based to Result<T, String> error handling
description: A Rust library uses unwrap() on parse operations. Migrate all three public functions to return Result<T, String> instead of panicking.

task_spec.prompt:
The Rust library in src/lib.rs has three functions that use unwrap() and will panic on invalid input:
  parse_int(s: &str) -> i32
  parse_pair(s: &str) -> (i32, i32)
  parse_and_sum(s: &str) -> i32

Migrate all three to return Result<T, String>:
  pub fn parse_int(s: &str) -> Result<i32, String>
  pub fn parse_pair(s: &str) -> Result<(i32, i32), String>
  pub fn parse_and_sum(s: &str) -> Result<i32, String>

Map parse errors to a descriptive String error. Use the ? operator to propagate errors from parse_pair to parse_and_sum.

Update the existing tests to call .unwrap() or .expect() on the Result. Add 2 new error-case tests:
  test_parse_int_invalid — parse_int("abc") returns Err
  test_parse_pair_invalid — parse_pair("x, y") returns Err

cargo test must pass all 5 tests. cargo build must succeed.
required_artifacts: Existing tests updated to unwrap Results
followup_prompts: Run `cargo test` to verify the migration is correct. Make sure existing behavior is preserved and the migration handles edge cases safely.
Final verification: run `cargo test` and confirm all tests pass. Is this migration safe to run on real data without data loss or breaking existing clients?
